VERS. 1.-- *Joatham was five and twenty years old,* [0688C] etc. At the beginning and at the end he numbers the years of Joatham, because as he began with justice, so he persevered unto the end. Whence the times of his life are proclaimed as worthy of praise.

VERS. 3.-- *He himself built the gate,* etc. Which in the Acts of the apostles is called Beautiful, and which according to the Hebrews and by them is called even to this day the gate of Joatham (because he himself built it).

*Ophel.* It was a tower not far from the temple, of wonderful height. Whence also it received the name Ophel, that is, of darkness or of cloud. But where it is written in Micheas: *And the tower of the flock, cloudy, of the daughter of Sion [n: (Mich. IV, 8)]*: in the Hebrew it has, *the tower Ophel.* The tower Ophel signifies the eminence of Scripture, which, founded upon history, buries the head of its spiritual sense among the clouds, while it hides the greatness of knowledge [0688D] from the eyes of men. Whence: *He made darkness his covert [n: (Psal. XVII)]*. Joatham, whose life is praised, signifies Christ, of whom it is said: *Great is the Lord and exceedingly to be praised [n: (Ibid., XLVII)]*, etc. For Joatham is interpreted consummated or perfect, and the Apostle says of Christ: *And being consummated, he became to all that obey him the cause of eternal salvation,* etc. [n: (Hebr. V)]. He himself built the high gate of the house of the Lord, and wrought the mystery of his incarnation with wonderful power, who says of himself: *I am the door. By me if any man enter in, he shall be saved [n: (Joan. X)]*. This gate was called high, of which the Psalmist says: *The Lord is high above all nations [n: (Psal. CXII)]*, etc.

## CHAPTER XXVIII.

[0689A]

VERS. 3.-- *In the valley of Benennom.* [n: (RAB.)] This is the valley of Benennom, etc., *as far as* for all of them that commit adultery, their hearts are as an oven.

## CHAPTER XXIX.

VERS. 3.-- *In that same year,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] Not otherwise would he imitate David his father, who from infancy, being given to God, magnified the worship of God in the beginning of his reign.

But morally he admonishes the rulers of the Church, that they be not slothful in the office committed to them, but do all things diligently.

Mystically Ezechias, who not only performed the work of God strenuously by himself or by his own men, but rather stirred up others by messengers to a like zeal, signifies Christ, [0689B] which the interpretation of his name also testifies. For Ezechias is laying hold of the Lord, or the strength of the Lord. But Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God, who washed away by his blood all the transgressions of the fathers which had been under the law, and plainly restored the worship of piety in the Church. He himself sent legates to call together the nations unto the faith. First the prophets, then the apostles, and their successors: he appointed the pasch to be celebrated in the second month; because, the shadow of the law ceasing, he taught that the true pasch was to be kept, of which Paul says: *For Christ our pasch is sacrificed [n: (I Cor. V)]*.

VERS. 6.-- *Our fathers have sinned,* etc. [n: (HIERON., quaest. in Paral., tom. III.)] This is written fully, etc., *as far as* and they adored toward the rising of the sun.

## CHAPTER XXX.

[0689C]VERS. 1.-- *He sent also,* etc. [n: (HIERON.)] When he had publicly sent messengers to all Israel, he sent secretly to Manasses and Ephraim, to those whom he knew could be converted by letters. For they were the prouder because of the royal dignity which was in the house of Ephraim.

## CHAPTER XXXI.

VERS. 1.-- *They broke the images,* etc. After the coming of the Saviour, not only in Jerusalem and in Juda, but in all the nations of the world idolatry was destroyed, and the pride of the devil fell. And as the number of the faithful increases, the worship of demons decreases, until at the end of the world the last death be overwhelmed, and the Lord alone shall reign in that day.

## CHAPTER XXXII.

[0689D]VERS. 4.-- *They stopped up all the fountains.* For those fighting against pagans and heretics, diligent caution must be used, and the mysteries must be veiled, whence: *Give not that which is holy to dogs, neither cast pearls before swine.*

VERS. 5.-- *He built.* [n: (RAB. in Paral. )] Christ built the Church which is the city of God, etc., *as far as* and he appointed teachers, the leaders of spiritual wars.

## CHAPTER XXXIII.

VERS. 12.-- *And he did penance exceedingly before the God of his fathers.* [n: (RAB.)] The penance of Manasses being heard, no man ought to despair of the mercy of God, but rather to presume of pardon through penance.

## CHAPTER XXXIV.

[0690A]

VERS. 5.-- *The bones moreover.* [n: (RAB.)] Therefore he burned the priests upon the altars of the idols, that he might show that the sacrifices of those men were deadly, who not only offered victims of cattle to demons, but delivered up even themselves to idolatry. Here he signifies all those who, made over to the service of the devil, have ended a sacrilegious life in time, as men to be consumed with eternal torments according to the desert of each.

VERS. 22.-- *To Olda the prophetess,* etc. [n: (HIERON.)] Olda was the wife of Sellum the uncle of the father of Jeremias, and the father of Ananeel. She dwelt in the second. It was a place of Jerusalem outside the wall of the city and the outer wall, which was called the second: of which mention is made in the prophet Sophonias.



## CHAPTER XXXV.

[0690B]

VERS. 1.-- *And Josias made in Jerusalem,* etc. [n: (RAB.)] We are admonished to purge first the ground of our heart from all vices, and so to celebrate the pasch to the Lord, *not with the old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness: but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth [n: (I Cor. V)]*. But mystically Josias, that is, the strength of the Lord, signifies Christ, of whom it is read: *The Lord strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle [n: (Psal. XXIII)]*. Josias is also interpreted the salvation of the Lord, and *Christ saves his people from their sins [n: (Matth. I)]*. He it is who with the zeal of God cleanses the land of Juda and Jerusalem from all uncleannesses, who said through the prophet: *The zeal of thy house hath eaten [0690C] me [n: (Psal. LXVIII)]*. Of whom elsewhere: *Whose fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his floor [n: (Matth. III)]*. He celebrates the true phase in the eighteenth year of his reign: because in the eighth age, the general resurrection being granted, he leads his saints with the perfection of good works to the penny of eternal blessedness, all scandals having first been cast out of his kingdom.

VERS. 3.-- *Put the ark in the sanctuary of the temple, which Solomon the son of David king of Israel built.* The Hebrews hand down that the ark was carried out of the temple in the time of Achaz, when idols had been put by him in the temple, and that it was brought over into the house of Sellum the husband of Olda, the uncle of Jeremias. For it could not be together with the idols.

[0690D]VERS. 18.-- *There was no Phase like to this,* etc. Because, the figures being taken away in the day of judgment, the saints shall pass from death to life, from corruption to glory, and in the sight of their Creator in the heavenly Jerusalem they shall rejoice for ever: because the God of gods shall be seen in Sion, because he hath made his mercy wonderful in the fortified city.

VERS. 21.-- *To which God commanded me to go in haste.* Because from the words of Jeremias and of the other prophets he was able to know the will of the Lord, by which judgment was to be passed upon a sinful people. Whence Rabsaces also said of Sennacherib king of the Assyrians: *The Lord commanded me to go up to the land [n: (Psal. LXXXIII)]*, because the prophets had foretold that he would go up, which was by no means hidden from him

VERS. 22.-- *In the field of Mageddo.* The slaying of Josias, [0691A] who was slain by Pharao Nechao in Mageddo, signifies the persecution of the ancient enemy against the preachers, whom he strives to deliver to death and to take away from the Church, that he may the more easily invade and scatter the whole people. For Pharao is interpreted scattering, Nechao striking, Mageddo of temptation. For the devil is permitted to rise up against the saints: and he contends with all his strength for this, that by tempting and striking the flock of God he may first take them away by scattering them, by whose comfort others fight against the enemy.

## CHAPTER XXXVI.

VERS. 4.-- *And he appointed.* Nechao appointed Joakim king, and laid a fine upon the land of a hundred talents of silver: because the devil demanded the weight of service from the people of the lost, [0691B] that both in understanding and in speech they might be ready for his obedience.

*And he turned.* It is to be noted that of the same Joakim the son of Josias it is thus written in Kings: *Joakim slept with his fathers, and Joachin his son reigned in his stead [n: (IV Reg. XXIV)]*. Josephus however says: When the king of Babylon had entered the city, he by no means kept faith, but slew the strongest young men and those comely in beauty together with king Joakim, whom he commanded to be cast forth unburied before the wall. But his son Joachin he appointed king of the whole province. And those who were set in dignities, to the number of three thousand, he led into Babylon, among whom was Ezechiel, still a boy. This end therefore had Joakim the king, who lived ten and thirty years, and reigned [0691C] eleven years. But the successor of the kingdom of Joakim, a king by name Ononimus, reigned three months and ten days. And it is to be known that when once a man has made himself over to any vice, he will be liable to many masters. Whence Joakim, whom Pharao before compelled to pay tribute to himself, him Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon compels to serve three years. Nabuchodonosor signifies the same one that Pharao does; the prince, namely, of confusion and the ruler of these darknesses. And when the devil has compelled anyone to pay him the tribute of sin, he brings him wholly [0692A] into his own dominion, and exacts full service, by persuasion, namely, by delight, by consent, and by thought too, by speech, and by work.

[n: (HIERON., quaest. in Paral., tom. III.)] It is to be known that the name of this Joachin, etc., *as far as* being corrupted by the examples of their superiors they go with them into the prey of the devil.

VERS. 10.-- *But the king.* Sedecias signifies those who undertake the rule among the people of God: for Sedecias is interpreted the just one of the Lord. For they receive the seat of justice for the exercising of the works of justice, they receive the dignity of honour and of office, chiefly because they deserve to be called sons of Josias, that is, of the salvation of the Lord, through the grace of baptism and the anointing of chrism: but degenerating they slip back into the foulness of vices, and turn those [0692B] subject to them [cj: *se*; read *sibi*, "to them"] to impiety, and keep not the faith which they had promised to God, nor observe the covenants of peace with men. Such men the divine law daily, and the miracles of the prophets and of the apostles, admonish to withdraw from their sins and to return to the Lord through penance: but once hardened, they despise the words of salvation, whence God, being angered, sends against them the king of the Chaldeans, that is, the devil with his satellites, that is, the spiritual wickednesses, who, sparing no age, yielding to no dignity, carry over into Babylon, that is, into confusion, whomsoever they take; and they burn the house of the Lord, because they compel the faithful, who are the temple of God, to blaspheme. They destroy the walls of Jerusalem, when they cast down the watches of the shepherds, they burn the towers, when they burn up the prelates through unlawful desires [0692C]: they demolish everything precious, when they reduce to nothing those who applaud themselves upon the prerogative of virtue and of knowledge.

The end of the book of Paralipomenon is like to the beginning of the book of Esdras the priest: whence what we have expounded there, there is no need to repeat here. Concerning Cyrus also, how he signifies Christ, and what things are said of him, and what things are referred to him, we have expounded in Isaias.

[n: (RAB. ex Beda.)] Solomon built the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem in seven years, etc., *as far as* namely, and of the city of God from which they had been cast out, they receive.
